{{Quote|Rav still makes good ''tihaar''. Best painkiller there is.|Kal Skirata|<ref name="TC">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref>}}
'''''Tihaar''''' was a [[Color/Legends|colorless]] [[Alcohol/Legends|alcohol]] [[Spirit (alcohol)|spirit]], made by members of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] culture.<ref name="TMPaC" /> Clear,<ref name="ImpCom" /> and typically triple distilled, ''tihaar'' had a high alcohol content and strong taste<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> that often burned the [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]] and throat when ingested.<ref name="TC" /> Mandalorian folk humor claimed that the potent ''tihaar'' could be used for [[Grease/Legends|degreasing]] [[Engine/Legends|engine]] parts.<ref name="O66" /> ''Tihaar'' could be made from any [[Fruit/Legends|fruit]] that was readily available,<ref name="TMPaC" /> including the likes of [[Jewel-fruit (Mon Calamari)|jewel-fruit]]<ref name="TZ" /> or [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore's]] own [[varos]] fruit. Every ''tihaar'' was different, taking on the flavor of whatever fruit had been used to distill it.<ref name="ImpCom" /> ''Tihaar'' was traditionally served in a short [[Glass/Legends|glass]], sometimes over [[Water/Legends|ice]], to be enjoyed slowly.<ref name="FLT">''[[Friends Like These]]''</ref>

The Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] [[Rav Bralor]] was a noted distiller of ''tihaar'', favoring the use of small red fruits in its production.<ref name="TC" /> During [[Gender/Legends|his]] [[Time/Legends|time]] on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], Mandalorian ''[[Cuy'val Dar]]'' training [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeant]] [[Kal Skirata]] took to drinking a glass of ''tihaar'' every night to help him get to [[Sleep/Legends|sleep]];<ref name="TZ" /> Skirata's supply of ''tihaar'' was shipped to Kamino by [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], [[Clone template/Legends|template]] for the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|clone army]] in production on Kamino, aboard his [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']].<ref name="O66" /> Because of his [[Standard year/Legends|years]] on Kamino, Skirata developed a taste for ''tihaar'', drinking it during [[Clan Skirata|family]] meals,<ref name="TC" /> and during a meeting with the post-[[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] ''Mand'alor'', [[Fenn Shysa]].<ref name="ImpCom" />

Five-liter containers of ''tihaar'' could be purchased in the marketplace of the [[City/Legends|town]] of [[Enceri]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Mandalore.<ref name="O66" /> The [[Sheb Niktose]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] on [[Vlemoth Port/Legends|Vlemoth Port]], located within the Mandalorian settlement of [[Arumorut/Legends|Arumorut]], served glasses of ''tihaar'' for five [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] each. Arumorut resident [[Teroch/Legends|Teroch]] was a lover of ''tihaar'', drinking the potent spirit in addition to mugs of [[Black ale/Legends|''ne'tra gal'']]. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Teroch met with operatives of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] at the Sheb Niktose, who'd come to Vlemoth Port looking to enlist Mandalorian aid in defending [[Xorrn/Legends|Xorrn]] from the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. There, Teroch and the rebels drank several shots of ''tihaar'' together while discussing Arumorut's history.<ref name="FLT" />

==Behind the scenes==
''Tihaar'' was first introduced to ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] with an unnamed mention in the [[2004]] novel, ''[[Republic Commando: Hard Contact]]'' by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]]. The drink again featured and was named in [[Republic Commando: Triple Zero|''Triple Zero'']], ''Hard Contact''{{'s}} sequel, and the second entry in Traviss' [[Republic Commando|''Republic'' and ''Imperial Commando'' series]]. Thereafter, ''tihaar'' came to appear in every subsequent entry into the series, including [[Republic Commando: True Colors|''True Colors'']], [[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel|''Order 66'']], and ''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''. Traviss' ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' article, ''[[The Mandalorians: People and Culture]]'', also provided information about ''tihaar'', comparing the drink to a [[:Wikipedia:Eau de vie|eau de vie]], or [[:Wikipedia:Brandy#Fruit brandy|fruit brandy]].

Many real-word distilled fruit liquors fit the description of tihaar, including Italian grappa, Georgian chacha, Russian samogan, South Slavic rakija, or Polish śliwowica. What all these drinks have in common is that they all are distilled from fermented fruit and not aged in barrels, which gives them their lack of color and intense taste.
